# Engineering-review action item: a fully-pinned, reproducible snapshot of
# every package (direct AND transitive) actually installed in this
# project's working environment at the time this file was generated --
# via `pip freeze`, exactly, no manual editing of versions. This freezes
# CURRENT REALITY (the exact versions every result in this project's
# findings documents was actually produced against), not a modernized or
# upgraded set. `requirements.txt` remains the human-readable, grouped,
# commented list of DIRECT top-level dependencies -- use THIS file
# (`pip install -r requirements-lock.txt`) when exact reproducibility
# matters; use `requirements.txt` when you want the unpinned list with its
# grouping/rationale comments intact.
#
# HONEST CAVEATS FOUND WHILE GENERATING/MAINTAINING THIS FILE, reported
# rather than silently resolved:
#
# 1. `torch==2.13.0` here does NOT capture the `+cu130` local version
#    suffix `torch.__version__` reports at runtime in this environment
#    (`pip show torch` itself only reports the bare "2.13.0", even though
#    the interpreter reports "2.13.0+cu130") -- a real quirk of how this
#    wheel's metadata was published, not something this file can pin
#    around. `pip install torch==2.13.0` should resolve to an equivalent
#    build via the same default index this environment used, but bit-for-
#    bit wheel identity is not 100% guaranteed by this pin alone.
#
# 2. FOUR packages this environment has installed and actually needs were
#    NOT listed in `requirements.txt` -- all four now added there directly,
#    since leaving a real, active dependency undocumented is a correctness
#    gap: `python-dotenv`, `matplotlib`, `scipy`, and `roboflow`.
#
#    `roboflow==1.4.0` deserves its own note, because an EARLIER pass
#    through this same review got it WRONG and said so explicitly in this
#    file -- corrected here rather than left standing. That earlier check
#    used a column-0-anchored grep (`^import|^from`) against
#    `pitch_keypoint_detector.py` and concluded the package was unused,
#    since only `os, tempfile, cv2, numpy` appeared at the top of the
#    file. A later, more thorough pass -- tracing every import
#    TRANSITIVELY from `production/tests/` through `production/src/`, via
#    a full AST walk rather than a line-anchored grep -- found a real,
#    deliberately LAZY, function-local import inside `_get_model()`:
#    `from roboflow.models.keypoint_detection import KeypointDetectionModel`,
#    indented inside the function body specifically so the (heavy,
#    optional) package is only imported if a real `ROBOFLOW_API_KEY` is
#    configured and that function actually runs. A grep anchored to
#    line-start structurally cannot see an indented import; an AST walk
#    (or any full-file parse) does. `roboflow` IS a real, direct
#    dependency of running code and has been added to `requirements.txt`
#    accordingly -- the prior claim that it was safe to leave undeclared
#    was incorrect, not a judgment call that changed.
#
#    `matplotlib`/`scipy` are used directly by the reporting track's
#    visualizers (`player_visualizer.py`, `team_visualizer.py`,
#    `pitch_diagram.py`, `zone_explainer.py`) -- found by the same
#    transitive trace, not previously checked at all since they were
#    never imported by any test file DIRECTLY, only reached by following
#    local imports into `production/src/reporting/`.
#
#    All three newly-added packages (`roboflow==1.4.0`, `matplotlib==3.11.1`,
#    `scipy==1.18.0`) were verified against PyPI directly (not assumed):
#    real, published, not yanked, with wheel files compatible with
#    `ubuntu-latest` + Python 3.14 on x86_64 (the CI runner's actual
#    platform) confirmed to exist.
